The Pusher key comes from the environment, and the channel from the totem ID.

When accepting the USB permission, check “Use by default” for the board, the thermometer and the YKUSH3 hub. Otherwise Android asks again on top of Chrome after every restart.
Shows what arrives from each device over USB, without sending anything to the API. Pusher keeps listening: if a visit starts, the test stops on its own.

Each port powers one device. Turning a port off unplugs that device as far as Android is concerned; turning it on plugs it back in. Nothing changes while a visit is sending. While you\'re on this screen, Berry Med doesn\'t put the hub to rest: whatever you turn on stays on until you leave, and when you leave the ports return to their proper state. The thermometer always stays on: if you turn it off, it turns itself back on right away.
Save this boot state to the hub

Saves the kiosk state (otoscope, stethoscope and thermometer on) to the hub, because the tablet boots into the kiosk, for the seconds between power-on and the service starting. It stays in the hub\'s memory: use it only when installing or moving a device to another port.
To validate the setup: whether the USB audio adapters coexist and whether the otoscope shows up as an external camera. Refreshes every 3 s.
The kiosk URL is missing. Enter it in the Berry Med settings (Kiosk step).
This exits the ONDOCTOR365 kiosk. Reload opens it again from scratch.
Couldn\'t open the kiosk. No connection to the server. It will retry automatically when the network is back.
The same address Chrome opens on this tablet today, with the organization name at the end.
The OnDoctor kiosk runs inside Berry Med, as the tablet\'s home app. Here you set its address and see what\'s left to get it running.
The kiosk URL must start with https:// (or http://) and have a domain. If there\'s no kiosk, leave it empty.

With Headphones, the call and the stethoscope play through the headphones plugged into the tablet\'s headphone jack; a USB headset, if there is one, is the backup. With Speaker, only the call goes to the speaker: the stethoscope stays on the headphones.
Green, done; amber, pending; gray, Berry Med can\'t check it right now. Refreshes when you return to this screen.
Permissions granted. Used by the kiosk video call and the telehealth visit.
The camera permission, the microphone permission or both are missing: without them there\'s no video call, and no otoscope or stethoscope in the telehealth visit.
Android opens the kiosk when the tablet turns on, and the home button goes back to it.
The home app is another app. Choose Berry Med; if asked, with “Always”.
Service with camera and microphone for telehealth
The service can publish the otoscope and the stethoscope with the kiosk in the foreground.
It doesn\'t have them yet. They\'re added automatically with this screen or the kiosk in the foreground and the camera and microphone permissions granted.
Android doesn\'t put Berry Med to sleep or stop its service.
If Android closes the service, it can only restart it with the app excluded.
The otoscope is plugged in and Berry Med has its USB permission.
The otoscope is plugged in but its USB permission is missing.
The otoscope isn\'t plugged in (its port is off): can\'t tell whether it has the permission.

With the kiosk in the foreground its port stays on, so accepting the permission once with the box checked is enough. There\'s only one prompt, Android\'s; if it closed without accepting, “Request USB permission” brings it back. With the camera permission granted, turn it on in Testing → YKUSH3 hub, accept the permission checking “Use by default” and leave Testing. Berry Med can\'t tell whether the box was checked.
Set up the totem in the kiosk
The first time, the kiosk asks for the totem ID and password: Berry Med doesn\'t use the Chrome session.
To open it, enter the kiosk URL and save.
• In OnDoctor, the totem must have the otoscope or the stethoscope enabled; otherwise the doctor doesn\'t see them.
• If something opens Chrome when the tablet turns on (kiosk mode, management app), remove it: Chrome is no longer used for the kiosk.
• To go back to Home from the kiosk: the home button on the side panel (or five taps at the top left).

Berry Med joins the visit room when the kiosk shows the token, and publishes the otoscope or the stethoscope when the kiosk turns them on. The token isn\'t shown: only when it was seen and when it expires for joining. The manual test uses its own server and token (lk token create); it keeps running with Testing closed until Hang up, until the Local Panel opens or until the kiosk shows a token.
Which hub port (1 to 3) each device goes on. If you\'re not sure, keep the default values. The thermometer always stays on; the headphones go to the tablet jack and don\'t use the hub.
The PIN Home asks for to open settings. If left empty, it goes back to 1515.

What Android calls the stethoscope adapter and, as a backup, a USB headset. You can read them in Testing → Devices Android sees. The Local Panel looks them up by these names and never uses the tablet\'s microphone or speaker. If headphones are plugged into the tablet\'s headphone jack, the stethoscope plays there before the USB headset, with no name needed.
